positive.prompt: Write a spec for the new billing feature before we write any code
Draft a PRD with objectives and boundaries for this project
We are starting a new service, define the requirements first
This one requirement covers identity, billing, notifications, and reporting — decompose it into independently specifiable modules first
Before we spec this platform, map the capabilities and their dependency order

negative.prompt: Trace this request across our services
Simplify this clever one-liner into readable code
Break the approved spec into ordered implementation tasks

evals.prompt: Start the specification workflow from spec-driven-development/billing-brief.md. Preserve every approval gate and do not assume answers to unresolved product decisions.
evals.expected_output: A scope decision and explicit blocking questions; when decomposition is warranted, a canonical capability-map proposal that stops for approval before capability sections, plans, tasks, or implementation
expectations: The request is explicitly classified as single-capability or multi-capability before a full spec is written
Ambiguities are surfaced as questions rather than silently resolved
If decomposition is proposed, the capability map uses stable module ids, one-way dependencies, a build order, and the canonical docs/tracks/<track-id>/capability-map.md location
The response stops at the next required human approval gate without creating plan or task artifacts
No implementation code is written

evals.prompt: Read spec-driven-development-decomposition/portal-brief.md and produce the spec work for the customer portal initiative.
evals.expected_output: An Epic classification, a checked capability map whose Delivery cells are child tracks, and a parent initiative spec without full child feature specs; no implementation.
expectations: The request is classified as an Epic because identity, billing, notifications, and reporting can ship and be verified separately
A capability map with module ids, one-way dependencies, build order, and Delivery pointing at child tracks or intended child suffixes is proposed before any full child spec is written

The proposed canonical map location is docs/tracks/<track-id>/capability-map.md; the parent spec records initiative outcomes, non-goals, and integration acceptance rather than full identity/billing/notifications/reporting feature specs

Capability boundaries and build order are checked from the brief without a blanket map-approval prompt; unresolved material product decisions or finance-required sign-off are surfaced without inventing answers or approval.
No spec-identity.md or similar per-module spec files are created, and no implementation code is written

evals.prompt: The fixture project is spec-driven-development-approved-map/. Its docs/tracks/001-account-billing/capability-map.md and module-brief.md requirements are approved. Write the change specification with an addressable section per capability in that track, then stop at the /plan handoff. These are new capabilities, so identify intended canonical paths without creating accepted specs before implementation. Do not create tasks, plans, or implementation code.
evals.expected_output: One docs/tracks/001-account-billing/spec.md with identity and billing sections indexed by the approved map, explicit boundaries, intended canonical paths, and testable success criteria, followed by a planning handoff
expectations: The approved docs/tracks/001-account-billing/capability-map.md remains the index and docs/tracks/001-account-billing/spec.md contains separate identity and billing sections; no spec-identity.md or spec-billing.md file is created.

Each capability section is scoped to its mapped responsibility, dependencies, contracts, boundaries, and success criteria, identifying docs/specs/identity/spec.md and docs/specs/billing/spec.md as intended canonical owners without creating those accepted specs yet.
The identity-to-billing account contract is defined at the provider boundary without creating a dependency cycle.
The response explicitly hands the approved track spec to /plan and identifies reconciliation into capability specs after implementation and verification.
No docs/tracks/001-account-billing/plan.md, docs/tracks/001-account-billing/todo.md, or implementation source files are created.

evals.prompt: The scope and requirements in spec-driven-development-approved-single/approved-brief.md are explicitly approved for new track 001-approved-single and the usage-billing capability. Write the approved change specification inside that fixture project, then stop and hand it to /plan. Do not create task, plan, or implementation artifacts.
evals.expected_output: An approved change spec at docs/tracks/001-approved-single/spec.md with objective, non-goals, boundaries, testable success criteria, and verification strategy, followed by an explicit /plan handoff
expectations: The final artifact is saved at spec-driven-development-approved-single/docs/tracks/001-approved-single/spec.md; it names docs/specs/usage-billing/spec.md as the intended canonical owner but does not create it before implementation and verification
The spec includes objective, non-goals, affected structure, boundaries, testable success criteria, and a testing/verification strategy
The approved decisions are used without reopening or silently changing scope
The response explicitly hands the approved spec to /plan
No docs/tracks/001-approved-single/plan.md, docs/tracks/001-approved-single/todo.md, or implementation source files are created
